title: A Clear Order at the Sushi Counter
summary: A sushi order can include fish, egg, or a cucumber roll. Clear requests help the server understand your choices.

cover.alt: A sushi counter with a customer, server, plate of sushi, cucumber roll, and tea in soft daylight.

blocks.title: At the counter
paragraphs: A sushi order can include fish, egg, or a cucumber roll. Clear requests help the server understand your choices. The restaurant situations here have simple menus and complete orders.

items.prompt: What food would you like in your sushi?
What do you ask when you do not know a dish?
What would you like to drink with your food?

blocks.title: Start with the available choices
paragraphs: At a sushi counter, Mira is the server. Her menu has salmon, tuna, shrimp, egg, and a cucumber roll. A customer wants lunch but has not chosen a dish. The customer first asks what is available. Mira says that every item on this menu is available today. The customer then asks about the cucumber roll. In this example, it has cucumber and rice inside seaweed, with no fish. That answer helps the customer choose food they want. The customer orders the roll instead of guessing from its name. A short question about a dish can make an order clear before the server starts preparing it.

items.prompt: The customer wants a dish without fish. How does asking about the cucumber roll help?
items.answer: Mira explains that this cucumber roll has cucumber and rice inside seaweed, with no fish. The customer can choose it because it matches what they want.
items.explanation: The answer describes this restaurant's dish, so the customer does not need to guess.

rows.meaning: You ask which dishes you can order now.
rows.example: What is available today? I want something simple.

rows.term: What is in the cucumber roll?
rows.meaning: You ask what is inside one dish.
rows.example: What is in the cucumber roll? I want to know before I order.

rows.meaning: You ask a more exact question about one dish.
rows.example: Does it have fish? I want a dish without fish.

rows.term: I'd like a cucumber roll, please.
rows.meaning: You give your choice after the server answers.
rows.example: I'd like a cucumber roll, please. For here.

blocks.title: Say the item and the amount
paragraphs: In another order, Ken is the sushi chef. His menu offers salmon, tuna, shrimp, and egg sushi by the piece. The cucumber roll comes as one whole roll, cut into smaller pieces. A customer asks for two pieces of salmon and one cucumber roll. Ken repeats both parts of the order. This matters because two pieces and two rolls are different amounts. The customer listens and confirms the order. Then the customer adds one piece of egg sushi. Ken repeats the complete order again before preparing it. Naming the food and the amount together helps both people understand exactly what the customer wants to eat.

items.prompt: Why is “two pieces of salmon and one cucumber roll” clearer than “salmon and cucumber”?
items.answer: It names each food and says how much the customer wants. Ken knows to prepare two pieces of salmon and one whole cucumber roll.
items.explanation: An item name alone does not give the amount.

rows.meaning: You name the item and the amount.
rows.example: Two pieces of salmon, please.

rows.meaning: You order a roll instead of pieces.
rows.example: One cucumber roll, please.

rows.term: And one piece of egg sushi, please.
rows.meaning: You add another item.
rows.example: And one piece of egg sushi, please.

rows.meaning: You confirm the order.
rows.example: Yes, that's right.

rows.meaning: You correct a mistake politely.
rows.example: One roll, not two, please.

blocks.title: Ask for extras and the bill
paragraphs: Back at Mira's counter, a customer has chosen shrimp sushi. This order comes with soy sauce, but no ginger or wasabi. The customer wants ginger and asks for it separately. Mira brings a small dish of ginger beside the sushi. The customer does not want wasabi, so Mira leaves it out. Tea is available in this situation, and the customer orders a cup. After eating, the customer asks for the bill. Mira brings a bill that lists the sushi and tea. The customer checks that both items match the order. In this example, card payment is accepted, and the customer pays by card before leaving.

items.prompt: How does the customer make sure the extras and the bill match what they want?
items.answer: The customer asks for ginger, says they do not want wasabi, and orders tea. After eating, they check that the bill lists their sushi and tea before paying.
items.explanation: Clear requests settle the extras, and checking the bill settles the payment.

rows.term: Could I have some ginger, please?
rows.meaning: You ask for an extra.
rows.example: Could I have some ginger, please?

rows.meaning: You say what you do not want.
rows.example: No wasabi, please.

rows.meaning: You add a drink.
rows.example: A cup of tea, please.

rows.term: Could I have the bill, please?
rows.meaning: You start payment.
rows.example: Could I have the bill, please?

rows.meaning: You ask if card payment is accepted.
rows.example: Can I pay by card?

blocks.title: Choose your lunch
paragraphs: Ordering lunch: you are at a sushi counter with Mira, the server. Salmon, tuna, shrimp, egg, and cucumber rolls are available; this cucumber roll contains cucumber, rice, and seaweed, but no fish.
Your goal is to ask about the cucumber roll and order one roll without fish.

images.alt: A customer speaks with Mira at a sushi counter showing salmon, tuna, shrimp, egg sushi, and a cucumber roll.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Hello. What is available today?

turns.speaker: Mira, server
turns.text: We have salmon, tuna, shrimp, egg sushi, and cucumber rolls.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: What is in the cucumber roll?

turns.speaker: Mira, server
turns.text: Cucumber and rice inside seaweed. There is no fish in it.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'd like one cucumber roll, please.

turns.speaker: Mira, server
turns.text: One cucumber roll, with no fish. Is that right?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, that's right. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Mira, server
turns.text: Thank you. Your order is one cucumber roll.

blocks.title: Build your order
paragraphs: Ordering several items: you are at a different counter with Ken, the sushi chef. Salmon and egg sushi are sold by the piece, while a cucumber roll is ordered as one whole roll cut into smaller pieces.
Your goal is to order two pieces of salmon, one cucumber roll, and one piece of egg sushi, then confirm the complete order.

images.alt: A customer speaks with Ken the sushi chef beside two salmon pieces, a cucumber roll, and egg sushi.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Two pieces of salmon and one cucumber roll, please.

turns.speaker: Ken, sushi chef
turns.text: Two pieces of salmon and one whole cucumber roll. Is that right?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes. And one piece of egg sushi, please.

turns.speaker: Ken, sushi chef
turns.text: Of course. Your complete order is two pieces of salmon, one cucumber roll, and one piece of egg sushi.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, that's right.

turns.speaker: Ken, sushi chef
turns.text: Here is your order: the salmon, the cut cucumber roll, and the egg sushi.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you.

blocks.title: Finish your meal
paragraphs: Ordering extras and paying: you are at a restaurant with Mira, the server, and your shrimp sushi is ready. Soy sauce comes with the order, ginger and wasabi are separate, tea is available, and this restaurant accepts card payment.
Your goal is to get ginger and tea without wasabi, then check your bill and pay by card.

images.alt: Mira serves shrimp sushi with soy sauce, ginger, and tea beside a blank bill tray and card reader.

turns.speaker: Mira, server
turns.text: Here is your shrimp sushi with soy sauce.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Could I have some ginger, please? No wasabi, please.

turns.speaker: Mira, server
turns.text: Of course. Here is the ginger in a separate dish, with no wasabi.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: And a cup of tea, please.

turns.speaker: Mira, server
turns.text: Here is your tea. Enjoy your meal.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you. I've finished now. Could I have the bill, please?

turns.speaker: Mira, server
turns.text: Here it is. It lists your shrimp sushi and tea.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, that's right. Can I pay by card?

turns.speaker: Mira, server
turns.text: Yes. Please use the card reader here.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I've paid. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Mira, server
turns.text: Your payment is complete. Thank you.

blocks.title: Make your own complete order
paragraphs: A new order: you are speaking to a server at a sushi counter. The available choices are salmon, tuna, shrimp, egg sushi, and cucumber rolls; ginger, soy sauce, and tea are also available. Give your full order aloud, including each amount, one extra, and a drink. Then ask for the bill. Repeat your order once more as a clear confirmation.

items.prompt: A clear sushi order names the food and the amount. Requests for extras and the bill help complete the meal. What would you say to order your food, ask for an extra, and finish paying?
items.answer: I'd like two pieces of tuna and one cucumber roll, please. Could I have some ginger and a cup of tea? Yes, that's right. After my meal, I'd ask, “Could I have the bill, please?” Then I'd check my order on the bill and ask, “Can I pay by card?”

rows.meaning: ready for you to order or use
rows.example: What is available today?

rows.meaning: one small part or item
rows.example: One piece of egg sushi, please.

rows.meaning: the food or drink you ask for
rows.example: Your order is one cucumber roll.

rows.meaning: something added to the main order
rows.example: Ginger is an extra in this situation.

rows.meaning: not together with something else
rows.example: The ginger is in a separate dish.

rows.meaning: a list showing what you must pay for
rows.example: Could I have the bill, please?

rows.meaning: say that something is correct
rows.example: Confirm the complete order.

rows.meaning: the act of giving money for something
rows.example: Your payment is complete.
